title: Extract information from audio · Level 2
slo: Identify the structured information an audio analyzer can return from a call.

exercises.question_text: What can the portal show after audio analysis? Select all that apply.

options.rationale: The portal can show a transcript after analysis. It displays the spoken call content in writing.
The portal can show schema-based insights. These correspond to fields expected from the media.
The portal can display returned JSON results. JSON represents structured result data.

options.error_type: Confuses audio outputs with invoice fields
options.rationale: An invoice subtotal is one invoice-specific field. Portal audio results can include several different outputs.
options.better_fit: Use this when reviewing an invoice extraction result.

exercises.explanation: Correct. The portal can show transcripts, insights, and JSON results.

exercises.question_text: Which outputs can audio analysis provide? Select all that apply.

options.rationale: Audio analysis can provide transcriptions. They turn spoken content into written text.
Audio analysis can provide summaries. They capture important information from a recording.
Audio analysis can return key insights. A schema can organize useful details from a call.
OCR recognizes printed words in images and scanned pages. Audio analysis can return speech-related outputs instead.
options.better_fit: Use OCR for a photo of a receipt or printed page.

exercises.explanation: Correct. Audio analysis can return transcriptions, summaries, and insights.

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: Results could be reviewed before any analysis has produced them.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: Select and run the analyzer first, then review its outputs and JSON.

exercises.correct_answer: Select an audio analyzer run it on media review the outputs view JSON results
exercises.explanation: The analyzer must be selected and run before its outputs and JSON result can be reviewed.

exercises.question_text: Speech recognition turns spoken audio into ___.

parts.text: Speech recognition turns spoken audio into

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: The output type would be named incorrectly.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: Use text: OCR reads printed words in images, not spoken audio.

exercises.explanation: Speech recognition changes spoken audio into written text.

exercises.question_text: Mia needs to check whether an audio analyzer extracts a callback field from a recorded call before her team automates the workflow in code. What should she do?

options.text: Run the analyzer in the portal
options.rationale: The portal lets Mia run the analyzer and inspect returned fields. She can validate the callback field before automating.
OCR reads printed text in images. It cannot validate a callback field from recorded speech.
options.better_fit: Use OCR for an image containing printed words.

feedback.intrinsic: Mia would not learn whether the callback field is returned.
feedback.instructional: Use an audio analyzer for a call; OCR is for visible text.

options.rationale: An invoice schema holds invoice-related fields. A callback field is relevant to a voicemail-style audio schema.
options.better_fit: Use an invoice schema when extracting data from invoices.

feedback.intrinsic: The validation could omit the callback detail Mia needs.
feedback.instructional: Match the schema and analyzer to the call recording.

options.rationale: Attendee counting is a visual-meeting task. It does not test a callback field in audio results.
options.better_fit: Use it for a meeting image or video.

feedback.intrinsic: Mia would still not know whether the callback field was extracted.
feedback.instructional: Run the audio analyzer and inspect its fields.

exercises.explanation: Correct. Portal testing verifies the returned field before automation.

exercises.question_text: A support agency records calls and needs written records for follow-up. Which capability should its lead choose?

options.rationale: Audio transcription converts spoken calls into written records. Those records support follow-up work.
Basic OCR reads printed words in images. It does not transcribe callers' speech.
options.better_fit: Use OCR for scanned forms or photographs of printed text.

feedback.intrinsic: Staff would still need to listen to calls for the spoken details.
feedback.instructional: Choose transcription for recorded speech; OCR is for visible printed text.

options.rationale: Video attendance analysis identifies people in visual media. It cannot create written call records.
options.better_fit: Use it for a meeting recording when attendance is needed.

feedback.intrinsic: The agency would not receive the requested written call records.
feedback.instructional: Attendance is a video insight; calls need transcription.

options.rationale: Invoice extraction finds fields in invoices. It does not convert recorded speech into writing.
options.better_fit: Use it for invoice numbers, totals, and other invoice fields.

feedback.intrinsic: Callers' requests would remain unavailable as written records.
feedback.instructional: Use audio transcription for spoken calls, not invoice extraction.

exercises.explanation: Correct. Transcription provides written records of spoken calls.

exercises.question_text: The prebuilt analyzer ID for audio is ___.

parts.text: The prebuilt analyzer ID for audio is

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: The analysis would be configured for the wrong media type.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: Use prebuilt-audioSearch for audio, not the invoice or video analyzer IDs.

exercises.explanation: The prebuilt audio flow selects prebuilt-audioSearch.

exercises.question_text: Arrange the parts to form a correct statement.

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: The relationship between the schema and its fields would be unclear.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: Begin with the schema, then state that it can define the caller and callback number.

exercises.correct_answer: A voicemail schema can define the caller and callback number
exercises.explanation: A voicemail schema defines call-related fields, including caller and callback number.

exercises.question_text: Noah is building a program to analyze customer voicemail files. Which actions should he take to get structured audio results? Select all that apply.

options.rationale: The analyzer needs an accessible URL for the voicemail file. This provides its audio input.
The flow starts an asynchronous operation. Results are available after the operation completes.
Returned fields contain structured information from the audio. Noah should inspect them after completion.
prebuilt-invoice is for invoice input. A voicemail file requires the prebuilt audio analyzer.
options.better_fit: Use prebuilt-invoice when the input is an invoice.

feedback.intrinsic: Noah would not be set up to extract voicemail information.
feedback.instructional: Match the analyzer ID to audio: use prebuilt-audioSearch.

exercises.explanation: Correct. Provide the URL, run asynchronous analysis, and inspect the returned fields.

exercises.question_text: Formatted plain text that can accompany extracted content is ___.

parts.text: Formatted plain text that can accompany extracted content is

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: The output format would be confused with either speech content or structured data.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: Use Markdown for formatted plain text; use transcript for written spoken audio.

exercises.explanation: Markdown is formatted plain text that can be returned with extracted content. A transcript is specifically the written rendering of speech.

exercises.question_text: A support agent analyzes Ava's voicemail to plan a reply. Which results should the agent use? Select all that apply.

options.rationale: This result identifies the caller. It helps the agent know who needs a response.
This captures Ava's requested next step. It helps the agent plan an appropriate reply.
This is Ava's callback number. It provides a direct way to return her call.
Tax is an invoice amount, not a voicemail result. It does not help respond to Ava's request.
options.better_fit: Use tax when processing an invoice's extracted amounts.

feedback.intrinsic: The agent could focus on unrelated data instead of responding to Ava.
feedback.instructional: Use call-related results: caller, requested action, and contact details.

exercises.explanation: Correct. These results identify Ava, her request, and how to reach her.

exercises.question_text: A support manager needs the written words from a recorded call to assign follow-up work. Which output should she inspect?

options.rationale: A transcript contains spoken audio as written text. It lets the manager read what the caller said.

options.error_type: Confuses audio output with invoice field
options.rationale: An invoice subtotal is an amount from an invoice. It does not contain words spoken in a call.
options.better_fit: Use it when checking an invoice's extracted subtotal.

feedback.intrinsic: The manager would have no written account of the caller's request.
feedback.instructional: Inspect the transcript to read spoken words from a call.

options.error_type: Confuses audio output with video insight
options.rationale: A video attendee count reports who was present in a meeting. It does not provide a caller's spoken words.
options.better_fit: Use it when reviewing attendance in meeting video.

feedback.intrinsic: Follow-up could be assigned without knowing what the caller said.
feedback.instructional: A transcript answers what was spoken; attendance answers who was present.

options.error_type: Confuses call output with document output
options.rationale: Document text layout describes text positions on a document image. It is not a written call record.
options.better_fit: Use it when examining layout in a document image.

feedback.intrinsic: The manager would not receive the caller's words in writing.
feedback.instructional: For recorded speech, inspect the transcript.

exercises.explanation: Correct. The transcript provides the call's spoken words in written form.
